transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-07
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (PioneerHealth Head of ML), Tom Blake (CTO), Lena Ortiz (Procurement)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Renewal coming up in Jan; PioneerHealth is interested in expanding Dedicated capacity across two additional regions and extending contract term for discounted committed capacity. Concern around data residency and SOC2/ISO compliance, also want performance baseline for latency-sensitive triage use cases. Redwood to send pricing addendum and run short pilot benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick sound check, can you hear me?
[00:03] Aisha Rahman: yes, loud and clear.
[00:05] Tom Blake: good here.
[00:07] Maya Chen: awesome. so the agenda — quick renewal check-in, talk about capacity needs, regions, and any procurement/legal items. Daniel will cover the pilot/benchmark plan.
[00:18] Daniel Ortiz: hi all, yeah i'll keep the technical bit short then we can dive into specifics.
[00:22] Aisha Rahman: perfect, thanks. just to set context, our renewal is early january and we want to lock committed capacity and add two additional regions — eu-west and ap-southeast — for latency reasons. also need to confirm retention/PII posture for some of the triage models.
[00:40] Maya Chen: great, that's aligned with what I had from the account notes. on committed capacity, are you thinking about increasing the Dedicated GPU pool size or adding another pool by region?
[00:51] Tom Blake: likely both? we saw a 2.5x q3 spike and expect more as we roll out clinician-facing features. main ask is predictable throughput and ability to fail over between regions.
[01:05] Daniel Ortiz: for failover, we recommend cross-region routing with a primary and warm-failover region. that keeps cold start times low. we can also provision reserved capacity in both regions if you want firm SLOs.
[01:18] Aisha Rahman: how does that factor into pricing? we are sensitive to unit costs; we don't want a huge uplift for warm standby.
[01:27] Maya Chen: good question. there's two levers — reserved committed capacity (monthly commit) which gives best unit economics, and burst/buffer capacity for failover which is cheaper if used rarely. we can model a hybrid: commit to base throughput across three regions, add small burst buffer in ap-southeast. i'll include scenarios in the addendum.
[01:43] Lena Ortiz: procurement note — we'll need a contract amendment template showing the new regions and term extension. can you add a 24-month/36-month pricing option? longer terms might get better rates.
[01:54] Maya Chen: yes, we can do both 24- and 36-month terms and show incremental discounts.
[01:58] Tom Blake: on compliance, any blockers for data residency? some of our PHI-adjacent logs must remain in eu-west for european customers.
[02:08] Daniel Ortiz: we support region-specific data residency for logs and KV cache; for Private deployments we can offer full on-prem or VPC with customer-managed KMS. for Hosted/Dedicated, we can ensure logs and traces are retained in region X with encryption at rest via your KMS.
[02:24] Aisha Rahman: is the SOC2/ISO attestation current in your security pack? procurement will want SOC2 report plus penetration test summary.
[02:33] Maya Chen: yes, our compliance pack is up-to-date. i'll attach SOC2 type II and ISO 27001 certs in the doc we send. also we have an audit log export option and SSO/SAML support with SCIM provisioning.
[02:46] Lena Ortiz: perfect. also want to confirm retention windows — 30 days vs 90 days — that affects cost.
[02:53] Daniel Ortiz: cost impacts yes, but we also recommend configurable retention per route, so you can keep sensitive routes shorter.
[03:00] Aisha Rahman: excellent. Daniel, for the pilot/benchmark — what do you need from our side?
[03:05] Daniel Ortiz: minimal: a test-key and optionally a region access list. ideally we run a 4-hour burst test to simulate peak QPS and a 30-minute latency SLO test for the triage workflow. i'll run the benchmark from our side to your queue endpoints; we just need the endpoints whitelisted.
[03:21] Tom Blake: we can do that. our infra folks will handle whitelisting. what's typical latency for a 1k-token triage prompt on your Dedicated pools?
[03:30] Daniel Ortiz: on our current configs, median gen latency is ~180-220ms for 1k tokens on A100-equivalent Dedicated with continuous batching, but that varies with batch sizing and KV cache hit rate. we'll capture P50/P95/P99 in the benchmark.
[03:45] Aisha Rahman: ok good. also one risk: if we add more regions, will there be model-variant parity? we have some custom quantized variants in us-west; we need same model behavior in eu-west.
[03:56] Maya Chen: yes, model parity is a core focus — we replicate model builds and quantization profiles per region. Daniel, any notes on replication time?
[04:03] Daniel Ortiz: replication depends on model size; for our common 13B quantized builds it's typically <6 hours with our fast sync. for larger models, plan 12-24 hours. we version pin so your traffic stays on the same build during rollout.
[04:17] Lena Ortiz: procurement question again — what's the SLA we can expect if we sign dedicated capacity?
[04:22] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency guardrails. i'll include the SLA doc; standard is 99.9% for Dedicated. higher SLAs are available with advanced support.
[04:33] Tom Blake: are there any network egress or inter-region costs we should plan for?
[04:38] Daniel Ortiz: you'll see egress between regions if you route across regions; we can minimize by colocating models and caches. we'll include an estimated egress model in the pricing scenarios.
[04:50] Aisha Rahman: great. let's talk timeline: we want the new regions live by late q1. is that feasible?
[04:57] Maya Chen: yes, provided legal signs in december and we provision capacity in january. lead time for Dedicated pools is typically 4-6 weeks per region; with overlap we can hit late q1. pilot should happen this month to validate latency.
[05:11] Tom Blake: ok — pilot this week if possible.
[05:14] Daniel Ortiz: I'll propose three windows, but need endpoint whitelists; i'll follow up.
[05:20] Maya Chen: perfect. any other blockers?
[05:22] Aisha Rahman: one more — can you share a sample addendum that shows committed tokens/GPU hours vs overages? procurement wants to model cost predictability.
[05:33] Maya Chen: yes, the addendum will include committed capacity, overage rates, burst pricing, and options for 24/36 months.
[05:40] Lena Ortiz: and please include termination clauses and data deletion timelines.
[05:44] Maya Chen: will do.
[05:46] Tom Blake: are you able to show a quick snapshot of our current usage and potential seat savings with increased batching/kv cache?
[05:54] Daniel Ortiz: i can, at a high level — right now your average tokens per request and hit rate suggest we could save ~18% with smarter batching and prefix KV caching, but the exact number will come from the pilot.
[06:08] Aisha Rahman: ok awesome.
[06:11] Maya Chen: recap / next steps: i'll send the pricing scenarios + addendum and compliance pack by tuesday (2026-11-10). Daniel will schedule bench windows and run tests; Aisha will share region list and whitelist details by Thursday (2026-11-12).
[06:25] Tom Blake: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:28] Maya Chen: thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot.
[06:32] Meeting ends (approx 16:42 PST)
